entries.meaning: The highest point of something, especially of success. ---
examples: That season was the pinnacle of his career.
The cathedral's stone pinnacles were rebuilt after the storm.
She reached the pinnacle of her field before she was forty.

entries.meaning: A card game for two to four players using a special forty-eight-card deck. ---
examples: My grandparents played pinochle every Sunday.
He taught the whole table how to play pinochle.
There's a pinochle league at the senior center.
entries.contrast: Spelled with -chle but said PEE-nuk-ul.

entries.meaning: A toy made of paper blades on a stick that spin in the wind. ---
examples: She stuck a pinwheel in the flowerpot by the door.
The kids ran down the beach with pinwheels.
The pinwheel barely turned in that breeze.

entries.meaning: A tiny white worm that infects the intestines, most often in young children. ---
examples: Half the preschool came down with pinworms.
A single dose of medicine clears up a pinworm infection.
Pinworms spread easily in day care.

entries.meaning: A feeling of irritation from having your pride hurt. ---
examples: He quit in a fit of pique over the seating chart.
She slammed the door out of pure pique.
There was a note of pique in his reply.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like peak and peek.

entries.meaning: Robbery at sea, or the illegal copying of software, films, or music. ---
examples: Software piracy costs the industry billions.
Piracy off that coast has dropped sharply.
The studio blames streaming piracy for the loss.

entries.meaning: A small sharp-toothed South American river fish that feeds in groups. ---
examples: The aquarium keeps a tank of piranhas.
A piranha is smaller than most people expect.
Guides say the piranhas here won't bother swimmers.
entries.contrast: The h is silent: puh-RAH-nuh.

entries.meaning: Someone who attacks and robs ships at sea. ---
examples: Pirates seized a tanker off the coast.
He dressed as a pirate for Halloween.
The museum has a whole room about Caribbean pirates.

entries.meaning: A full turn on one foot in ballet or figure skating. ---
examples: She finished the routine with a clean pirouette.
He can do three pirouettes in a row.
The pirouette is harder than it looks.

entries.meaning: The female part in the center of a flower, where seeds form. ---
examples: Pollen has to reach the pistil for the plant to make seeds.
We labeled the stamens and the pistil.
Some flowers have several pistils.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like pistol, the gun.

entries.meaning: A round flat bread that opens into a pocket. ---
examples: Stuff the chicken and salad into a warm pita.
We bought a bag of pitas and some hummus.
He toasts pita and eats it with olive oil.

entries.meaning: A hidden problem or mistake that is easy to run into. ---
examples: The guide lists the common pitfalls of buying a first home.
That assumption is a classic pitfall.
She warned us about one pitfall in the contract.

entries.meaning: The soft white layer under the peel of a citrus fruit, or the spongy core of a stem. ---
examples: Scrape off the pith — it's bitter.
The pith of the orange sticks to the segments.
Cut the stem open and you'll see the white pith.
entries.русский: белая мякоть под кожурой цитруса; сердцевина

entries.meaning: A very small amount of money, especially as pay. ---
examples: They pay the interns a pittance.
He sold the whole collection for a pittance.
Her pension is a pittance compared to the cost of rent.

entries.meaning: A small gland at the base of the brain that controls growth and other glands. ---
examples: The scan showed a small tumor on his pituitary.
The pituitary releases the hormone that triggers growth.
Damage to the pituitary can throw off the whole system.

entries.meaning: The fixed point something turns on, or a sudden change of direction or strategy. ---
examples: The lever turns on a steel pivot.
The company's pivot to software saved it.
Two quick pivots in strategy confused everyone.

entries.meaning: A particular point, area, or building. ---
examples: This is a good place to stop for lunch.
We looked in all the usual places.
Put it back in its place when you're done.

entries.meaning: A pill or treatment with no active drug in it, given to compare against a real one. ---
examples: Half the group got the drug and half got a placebo.
The pain went away even on the placebo.
Trials use placebos to rule out wishful thinking.

entries.meaning: Something put in temporarily until the real thing is ready. ---
examples: That title is just a placeholder.
The slides still have gray placeholders where the charts go.
I put a placeholder on the calendar for Thursday.

entries.meaning: The act of putting something in a particular position, or the position chosen. ---
examples: The placement of the outlets is all wrong.
She's happy with her job placement after graduation.
They tried three different placements for the couch.

entries.meaning: The organ that forms in the womb to feed a growing baby and is delivered after birth. ---
examples: The placenta came out about ten minutes later.
The ultrasound checked where the placenta was sitting.
In mammals the placenta does the work the eggshell can't.

entries.meaning: A tiny cell fragment in the blood that helps it clot. ---
examples: Her platelet count came back low.
Platelets clump together to plug the cut.
He donates platelets every few weeks.

entries.meaning: A dull, obvious remark that has been said too many times to mean much. ---
examples: The speech was twenty minutes of platitudes.
Don't give me a platitude about hard work.
Every platitude about teamwork showed up on that poster.

entries.meaning: The playing of a recording that has just been made or stored. ---
examples: The guitar sounded fine on playback.
Playback keeps stuttering on my old phone.
Hit the button to start playback from the beginning.

entries.meaning: A book of a team's set plays, or a standard set of tactics for handling a situation. ---
examples: Every rookie has to learn the playbook by camp.
That move came straight out of the startup playbook.
The two companies are running the same playbooks.

entries.meaning: A rich man who spends his time on parties, travel, and short relationships. ---
examples: He had a reputation as a playboy in his twenties.
The novel is about a bored playboy and his driver.
The tabloids called them a pair of aging playboys.

entries.meaning: A polite remark made to be friendly rather than to say anything real. ---
examples: We exchanged pleasantries and got down to business.
He managed one stiff pleasantry before leaving.
The call was two minutes of pleasantries and nothing else.

entries.meaning: A serious promise, often to give money or to act in a certain way. ---
examples: The station collected over a thousand pledges during the drive.
She made a pledge to donate half her salary.
His campaign pledge was to cut property taxes.

entries.meaning: A difficult and troubling situation someone is stuck in.
examples: The article describes the plight of workers left without pay.
Nobody in charge seemed to notice their plight.
The film compares the plights of two families.
entries.contrast: The gh is silent: PLYTE, rhyming with night.
